subject: Finly discovery recap — p95 latency & streaming requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finly.com>, Dana Brooks <dana@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Finly discovery recap — p95 latency & streaming requirements

Thanks again for the time today — quick recap from our discovery so we have a shared checklist and next steps. Please reply with any corrections or additions.

High-level pain points you shared:
- Users report noticeable streaming lag in the product UX (first-token and incremental token latency).
- p95 latency spikes during peak hours causing degraded conversion in the editor flows.
- Current stack is brittle under concurrent streams; retries/backpressure cause duplicated requests and cost spikes.

Current stack & baseline metrics you gave:
- Using a managed API endpoint + homegrown streaming client.
- Typical request: ~250 tokens average, some up to 1k tokens.
- Peak concurrency today ~300 concurrent streams; peak QPS ~800.
- Observed p95 (end-to-end): ~1.6s on peak, streaming first-byte p95 ~700ms.

Success criteria you outlined:
- Streaming first-token p95 <= 500ms (for interactive flows).
- End-to-end response p95 <= 1s for 90% of calls; acceptable p95 SLA 99th <= 2s.
- Support sustained concurrency of 500+ simultaneous streaming sessions with graceful degradation above that.
- Predictable unit cost and ability to cap spend via routing/quantization.

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA):
1) Finly to share sample latency logs and one-week traffic profile (Samir) — done/attached if available.
2) Redwood to run an initial benchmark with a synthetic traffic profile that matches your token distribution (Aditya) — target week of Aug 3.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive to validate model family, seq lengths, and auth/integration (Marissa + Aditya) — propose Aug 3 or 4.
4) Exchange mutual action plan (MAP) and access for a read-only test harness (Marissa) — attaching initial MAP.

Attachments: Finly sample logs expected (please attach if available). I've attached an initial MAP template to kick off timeline/priorities.

Thanks — we should be able to show a short benchmark and a clear remediation plan in the follow-up call.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Looping in some quick technical checklist items so we can be prepared for the Aug 3 deep-dive and the initial benchmark run:

1) Model + inference details:
- Which model family are you running in prod/staging? (open-source Llama2-Chat, a hosted LLM, or internally fine-tuned variant?)
- Typical sequence lengths: you mentioned avg 220, 95th ~820 — confirm tokenization (BPE/other) and whether you use system prompts per request.

2) Traffic profile for benchmark:
- Provide 5-minute peak QPS snapshot and typical concurrency distributions (we need distributions of inter-arrival times).
- Confirm concurrent streams vs concurrent non-streaming requests.

3) Streaming UX metrics we will measure:
- First-byte p95 (time to first token)
- Incremental token latency (per-token p95 for long sequences)
- End-to-end p95 (finalized response)

4) Integration & auth:
- Which auth mechanism for staging (API key / mTLS / token broker)? We prefer read-only API keys scoped to the staging project.

5) Access for load testing:
- Please provide a read-only test key + optional staging endpoint host. If you prefer, we can run tests from your environment with an agent.

Preliminary suggestions based on the notes:
- Prioritize reducing first-byte p95: small-batch greedy execution + warm KV cache for common prefixes will help streaming UX.
- If you need cost reductions, we can evaluate quantized variants for higher throughput with small quality regressions on long-tail cases.
- Plan for graceful degradation: route new sessions to a cheaper model variant when capacity pressure crosses threshold.

If you can share the staging key before EOD Mon Aug 2, we'll run a short smoke benchmark and have results in time for the call.

Thanks — Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
